source_text: This incident bolstered the apostolic case against Judaizing demands, providing Peter—initially cautious about Gentile inclusion—with firsthand evidence of divine impartiality, later invoked at the Council of Jerusalem to argue that no yoke of circumcision or law observance should burden Gentile believers, as salvation came through grace as it had for Jews. [74] [72]
